# Results (auto-generated by train.py, version 20261002-191122)

Deployed model: **Logistic Regression**. XGBoost (tuned) minus Logistic Regression = -0.0002 AUC (95% CI [-0.0032, +0.0028], out-of-fold on train): XGBoost is not significantly better (CI includes 0) -> the simpler, directly interpretable Logistic Regression is deployed.

Neural-net / stacking models are benchmarks: they cannot give per-customer reasons, so they are only
deployable if a model-agnostic explainer is added.

## Business impact (assumed: churner loses 500, offer costs 50, offer keeps 30% of contacted churners)
| policy | contacted | cost | saving_vs_do_nothing | saving_pct |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Do nothing | 0 | 187000 | 0 | 0.0 |
| Offer everyone | 1409 | 201350 | -14350 | -7.7 |
| Random 20% of customers | 282 | 189870 | -2870 | -1.5 |
| Model: top 20% (call list) | 282 | 172000 | 15000 | 8.0 |
| Model: cost-optimal threshold 0.38 | 454 | 170700 | 16300 | 8.7 |

- Contact-worthy threshold in theory = offer/(loss*save) = 0.33; empirical (train out-of-fold) = 0.38.
- Break-even: the top-20% campaign pays off only if the offer success rate is above **15%**.
- Random targeting of 20% saves -2,870; the model call list saves 15,000.
- See `sensitivity.png` for savings at other success rates.
